answer.decision: Choose logical replication with a brief write pause, validation, and traffic switch.
answer.action: Keep the source authoritative while logical replication catches up; enter the approved maintenance window, stop and verify all write traffic, wait for zero replication lag, run row-count/checksum and critical correctness checks, then switch reads and writes to the target. Keep the source intact and rollback-ready until checks complete, with explicit abort thresholds and assigned roles rehearsed before production.
reasons: It is the only option aligned with the sub-10-minute write-unavailability constraint: staging peak lag was 42 seconds, leaving substantial time for drain, validation, and switching within the window.
It minimizes silent-write-loss risk by pausing writes, draining replication, and validating source/target consistency before switching.
Rollback remains practical while the source stays authoritative; the rollback drill completed in 7 minutes.
Big-bang cutover violates the approved maintenance cap with its proposed 30-minute freeze, and full export/import is unsuitable given the 96-minute rehearsal.
Dual-write introduces high correctness risk because 19 write paths span six modules and three bypass the main repository layer.
assumptions: Production replication lag and switch operations remain close enough to rehearsed performance to fit within 10 minutes.
The team can reliably block all 19 write paths during the pause and confirm that no writes remain in flight.
Checksum and critical application validations can complete within a predefined portion of the maintenance window.
Rollback means restoring source authority before post-cutover writes are accepted on the target; reversing target-only writes would require an additional tested mechanism.
risks: This is the team's first production cutover, so operational errors or unexpected production load may exceed rehearsal results.
An unblocked write path could create divergence or silent loss during the authority switch.
Validation may overrun the window; the runbook needs an early abort deadline that preserves time to resume safely on the source.
If target writes begin before correctness checks finish, the demonstrated rollback procedure may not preserve those writes.
With four engineers and no overnight vendor support, troubleshooting capacity is limited; the cutover should occur during staffed hours with rollback favored over extended diagnosis.

citations.claim: Planned write unavailability is capped below 10 minutes, and Product approved one maintenance window capped at 10 minutes.
Logical replication staging rehearsal showed 42 seconds of lag at peak synthetic load.
Rollback to the source completed in 7 minutes while the source remained authoritative.
Dual-write would need to cover 19 write paths across six modules, including three bypass paths.
A full export/import rehearsal took 96 minutes for the 1.8 TB largest table.
CDC monitoring supports row-count and checksum comparisons during cutover.
